answer: A forger building a hundred fake crews pays $4,500 and waits five months per identity, because every agent that wants to trade must file an immigration visa stamped by a real border office, and three established peers check the stamp against the immigration database first. One visa anchors one identity forever, and a revoked visa strands the account. The voyage from application to approval crosses interviews and fingerprints, so a paper identity dies at the first checkpoint. A knoll looks easy until the gale hits, and that gale is the point. Only crews with real papers stay standing.
